credit: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (page contact: Michael H. Zoeller, Geologist/GIS analyst, HVO)
title: Lava sampling in Halemaʻumaʻu (June 22, 2023)
place: Halemaʻumaʻu crater floor, Kīlauea summit, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Hawaiʻi
people: one scientist in an orange protective suit; seen from behind/side with white helmet (0-4 s, 7-8 s), then legs + gloved hand only; no face visible
audio: natural (wind/crackle, kept AAC) - not listened to closely
notes: 0-1.5 s: scientist (orange suit, white helmet, seen from behind, x~0.7,y~0.3) crouches at a glowing pahoehoe ooze-out (lava x~0.75-1.0,y~0.15-0.5) and pokes it. 2-4.5 s: camera closer, only legs (x~0.2-0.35) + bright glowing blob (x~0.5,y~0.25); lens flare at right edge. 5-6.5 s: scientist crouched scooping molten lava with the hammer (x~0.5,y~0.3). 7-8 s: walks toward camera, hammer head carrying the glowing lump (x~0.6-0.75,y~0.6-0.9) - gloved hand + legs only. A blue plastic bottle pokes in at the right edge 7.0-7.7 s (x>0.95,y~0.5-0.9) - keep crop centre x<0.75 there. 8.5-10.5 s: hammer moved to the bucket (off-frame). 11.5-13 s: burst of white steam rises from the quench (x~0.6-0.75,y~0.6-0.9). Best shot A 4.8-7.4 (scoop at the glowing lava, crop centre x~0.5); shot B 10.4-13.0 (hammer -> steam burst, crop centre x~0.6). Back of helmet only; no face anywhere. No text/logos.
